conditions.label: Infected gangrene of left lower extremity with nonrevascularizable critical limb ischemia

documents.title: Vascular surgery clinic
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Vascular Surgery Clinic
Patient: Lawrence Leary. Eight weeks after left below-knee amputation for infected gangrene with nonrevascularizable ischemia.
Home with home health. Pain minimal. No fevers.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: residual limb incision fully healed, no drainage, no erythema, good soft tissue cover, mild expected edema controlled with shrinker. Right foot: no wounds, faint pedal pulses.
Plan: limb ready for prosthetic casting - referral to prosthetics. Continue aspirin and statin. Right foot daily inspection and podiatry every 2-3 months. Vascular follow-up in 6 months or sooner for any right foot wound.
Vascular Surgery

documents.body:
Medical Oncology Follow-up
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (L2, L4), on leuprolide + enzalutamide since 10/2023.
Interval: left below-knee amputation in November for an infected ischemic foot; recovering at home.
No bone pain. Fatigue a bit more since surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSA <0.1 ng/mL.
Plan: continue both. Leuprolide given. PSA in 3 months, visit in 6.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, in wheelchair, came by van.
Year: cholecystectomy 5/2025 (acalculous cholecystitis), left BKA 11/2025 for infected gangrene, rehab, home health finished last week. Prostate cancer PSA undetectable. Left CRVO stable per retina.
Function: independent with transfers, toileting, dressing; walker hops in the apartment. Groceries delivered. Prosthetic casting scheduled next month. Fall screen: no falls since home.
Mood: PHQ-2 1. Says he is 'getting used to it'.
Prevention: vaccines current for the season. LDCT - he asked to skip this year with everything going on; we will revisit in the fall.
Exam: vitals as charted, weight lower post-amputation. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Residual limb healed. Right foot without lesions, vibration reduced.
Labs today.
Plan: same meds. Podiatry for right foot every 2-3 months. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Prosthetic fitting note
documents.author: prosthetics
documents.body:
Prosthetics and Orthotics - Delivery Note
Patient: Lawrence Leary, left transtibial amputation 11/19/2025.
Definitive-style left transtibial prosthesis delivered today after test socket check: total-contact socket, pin-lock liner, dynamic-response foot. Fit good, skin check after 20 minutes of standing without redness over the tibial crest or fibular head. Donning and doffing taught; wear schedule starting 1 hour twice a day, increasing as tolerated.
Outpatient PT for gait training ordered with the prescribing physician's approval.
Prosthetics

events.reason: Tearing chest pain to the back

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Widened mediastinum. Enlarged aortic knob. Lungs clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Widened mediastinum with enlarged aortic knob; aortic pathology should be excluded.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 88. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No ST elevation or depression. No T-wave changes.
reports.conclusion: LVH without ST or T-wave changes.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest. An intimal flap begins in the ascending aorta and ends before the origin of the innominate artery. Arch branch vessels and descending thoracic aorta without a flap. No pericardial effusion. Lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Type A aortic dissection confined to the ascending aorta.

reports.text: Intraoperative TEE. Dissection flap in the ascending aorta. Aortic regurgitation present. Left ventricular function normal. No pericardial effusion. Post-repair: competent aortic valve.
reports.conclusion: Ascending aortic dissection with aortic regurgitation; valve competent after resuspension.

documents.title: Cardiothoracic surgery discharge summary
documents.author: cardiothoracic surgery
documents.body:
Discharge Summary - Cardiothoracic Surgery
Patient: Lawrence Leary, 70 M
Admitted 05/20/2026 through the ED; ICU 05/20-05/24; discharged home 05/30/2026.
Diagnosis: acute type A aortic dissection with aortic regurgitation.
Operation: emergency replacement of the ascending aorta with resuspension of the aortic valve, 05/20/2026.

Presentation: sudden onset at home of severe tearing chest pain going through to the back, the worst pain of his life. Background: hypertension, diabetes, PAD with left below-knee amputation after a hospitalization for limb ischemia last November; also CKD 3, cecal angiodysplasia, prostate cancer (suspected per transferred list), CRVO, cholecystectomy.
ED: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 20. Diastolic murmur along the right sternal border. Extremities cool with diminished pulses in the lower extremities.
Labs: hemoglobin 14, WBC 9,000, platelets 250,000, creatinine 1.7, troponin I <0.04 ng/mL.
Chest film: widened mediastinum, enlarged aortic knob. ECG: LVH, no ST or T changes. CT angiogram: type A dissection beginning in the ascending aorta and ending before the innominate artery.

Course: taken directly to the operating room. Intraoperative TEE showed aortic regurgitation; ascending aorta replaced with a tube graft and the aortic valve resuspended, valve competent afterward. Extubated postoperative day 1. ICU through 05/24 for blood pressure control. Chest tubes out day 3. Creatinine stayed in his usual range. Started metoprolol succinate. Ambulating with his prosthesis and a walker with PT by discharge.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily; NEW metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: sternal precautions 6-8 weeks, no driving, no lifting over 10 lb. Blood pressure goal below 120/80.
Follow-up: cardiothoracic surgery in 3-4 weeks; primary care within 1 week; CT angiogram about 6 months after surgery.

Cardiothoracic Surgery

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 5/30 after emergency repair of an acute type A dissection (ascending aorta replaced, aortic valve resuspended) 5/20. Pain was sudden, tearing, into the back - called 911 himself.
Now: sternal soreness, sleeping in the recliner, appetite returning. Walking a little with the prosthesis and walker. No fevers, no shortness of breath.
Meds reconciled: new metoprolol succinate 50 daily, taking it. Rest of list same; enzalutamide continues (not on the hospital list). Leuprolide next due in July.
Exam: BP and HR as charted. Sternotomy incision clean, sternum stable. Heart regular, no murmur heard today. Lungs clear. Residual limb skin fine.
Labs today.
Plan: keep CT surgery appointment 6/23. Sternal precautions. Home health RN/PT re-ordered for 4 weeks. Home BP log on the new medicine.

documents.title: Cardiothoracic surgery post-operative visit
documents.author: cardiothoracic surgery
documents.body:
Cardiothoracic Surgery Clinic
Patient: Lawrence Leary, 70 M. Five weeks after emergency ascending aorta replacement with aortic valve resuspension for acute type A dissection.
Doing well at home. Mild incisional discomfort. No chest pain like the original event.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin, tamsulosin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: BP 128/76. Sternum stable, incision healed. Heart regular.
Plan: continue metoprolol; lifelong blood pressure control. Sternal precautions until 8 weeks. Repeat CT angiogram of the chest about 6 months after surgery (around November), then yearly. Cardiac rehab offered; he would prefer to continue his prosthetic PT for now.
Cardiothoracic Surgery

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months out from the dissection repair. Feels stronger. Home BP readings mostly in the 120s-130s over 70s since metoprolol. Walking with the prosthesis and a cane indoors now; outpatient PT twice a week.
DM: A1c today high 8s. Metformin twice daily.
Exam: BP and HR as charted. Sternal incision healed. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Right foot: skin intact, no ulcer, callus none, vibration reduced. Residual limb fine.
Labs: kidney function stable at his baseline.
Plan: continue metoprolol, HCTZ and the rest. CT angiogram is ordered by CT surgery for November. Flu/COVID in the fall. RTC 3 months.
